report.headline: Every part is answered. The fixes below will make it stronger.
report.summary: The answer successfully explains how wetlands lower flood peaks by storing water and slowing surface runoff. However, it lacks a discussion on the economic benefits of nature-based solutions and proactive legal protections. To improve, first clarify the specific mechanism of risk reduction and include a point on infrastructure cost-benefits.
report.question: Discuss how urban wetlands reduce flood risk and suggest ways to conserve them.

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.
Propose practical measures and say who should act and how.

sentences.text: Urban wetlands act as temporary reservoirs.
During intense rain they spread and store water, and release it slowly into streams, lowering the flood peak downstream.
When drains are blocked or wetlands are filled for construction, this storage and connectivity are lost.
Cities should first map the catchment, floodplain and inflows, then enforce no-fill buffers through development plans.
Restore blocked inlets and treat sewage before it reaches lakes.
Residents can map encroachments and report changes in water levels.
Drains and pumps still matter in exceptional storms; plans should track flood depths and drainage time before and after restoration.
